title: Simultaneous semilinear open tensor comparison on flat K-flat models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$ use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], $B_{n,T}=(A_n)_T$ and $\widehat R_T=\lim_nB_{n,T}$. Use the strict semilinear module-system category $\mathscr S_T$, derived reduction $\mathcal R_T\dashv\mathcal L_T$, and the actual unit $u$ and counit $e$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Completeness means the quotient-tower Roos-triangle condition of [def-weil-derived-complete], and normalized means that every transition-adjoint $N_m\otimes^L_{B_{m,T}}B_{n,T}\to N_n$ is invertible for $m\ge n$. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Identify $j^{-1}\widehat R_X=\widehat R_U$ and $j^{-1}B_{n,X}=B_{n,U}$. Write $j_!\dashv j^*$ for exact localized ringed-site extension and restriction, $J_j\dashv P_j$ for their termwise-system adjunctions, and $\eta^o,\epsilon^o,\eta^S,\epsilon^S$ for the respective units and counits [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

For every unbounded $K\in D(\widehat R_U)$ and every flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, lem-pc-kflat-resolution], $j_!Q$ is again flat-term K-flat and represents $j_!K$. For any complex $F$ on $X$, the ordinary slice tensor maps induce a natural chain isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Tot}(j_!Q\otimes F)\cong j_!\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes j^*F),$$
with direct sums in each total degree and differential $d_Q\otimes1+(-1)^a1\otimes d_F$ on the $(a,b)$ summand [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

The generator-normalized open tensor comparisons give an isomorphism of complexes of strict semilinear systems
$$r_Q:\bigl((j_!Q)\otimes_{\widehat R_X}B_{n,X}\bigr)_n\xrightarrow{\sim}J_j\bigl(Q\otimes_{\widehat R_U}B_{n,U}\bigr)_n.$$
On the summand of the extension presheaf indexed by a map to $U$, its $n$-th component is $[x]\otimes a\mapsto[x\otimes a|_U]$, followed by sheafification. It commutes before localization with every quotient transition and with both strict scalar-unit augmentations $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Its localization is a specified natural isomorphism
$$r_K:\mathcal R_X(j_!K)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_j\mathcal R_UK$$
in $D(\mathscr S_X)$, independent of $Q$ through the canonical computation comparisons. Its evaluation at every $n$ is the canonical derived open tensor isomorphism of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. The displayed representative square, its coefficient formulas and its naturality hold for the specified simultaneous section constructions of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], prior to scalar restriction; no lift of an arbitrary family of evaluated derived arrows is chosen. Neither completeness of $K$ nor quasi-compactness of $j$ is required.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] to identify the site of U with the slice at U of the site of X. Put O=\widehat R_X and O_U=j^*O. For module sheaves G on U and H on X, let P_G be the extension presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. On V, define a pairing P_G(V) times H(V) into j_!(G\otimes j^*H)(V) by ([x]_f,a)\mapsto[x\otimes a|_{(V,f)}]_f and extend additively over the summands f:V\to U. Balancing holds since O_U(V,f)=O(V); the formula respects restrictions because both x and a restrict along the same arrow. The bilinear sheafification extension theorem [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension-existence] and the sheaf tensor as sheafification of the presheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with the universal property of module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], therefore give a map \psi_{G,H}:j_!G\otimes H\to j_!(G\otimes j^*H). It is natural in G and H: both composites for a pair of module maps send [x]_f\otimes a to the extension summand of the tensor of their images. Uniqueness of bilinear extension [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension-uniqueness] makes these equal as sheaf maps.

source.place: Tag 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor), explicit forward generator map; sheafification of the extension presheaf

proof.text: Construct \kappa:j_!(G\otimes j^*H)\to j_!G\otimes H by the module adjunction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]: transpose G\otimes j^*H\xrightarrow{\eta_G\otimes1}j^*j_!G\otimes j^*H\cong j^*(j_!G\otimes H), using the pure-tensor restriction comparison [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction]. Explicitly, a map \alpha:G\to j^*L is extended by summing \alpha_{(V,f)} on the summands of P_G(V) and sheafifying [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. Conversely a map j_!G\to L restricts to each such summand; the two operations are inverse by the universal property of module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For L=j_!G and its identity this gives \eta_G(x)=[x]_f on (V,f); hence \kappa sends [x\otimes a]_f to [x]_f\otimes a. Thus \kappa\psi fixes every [x]_f\otimes a. Such elements determine a bilinear pairing after sheafification by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension-uniqueness], so \kappa\psi=1. For \psi\kappa, take the adjoint and precompose with the unit on G\otimes j^*H. On x\otimes a the resulting map is [x\otimes a]_f, which is precisely that unit. Pure tensors determine a tensor map [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and the adjunction is bijective; consequently \psi\kappa=1. This proves invertibility with the specified generator normalization rather than choosing an unspecified isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor), adjunction proof and explicit two inverse identities

proof.text: Apply \psi to G=Q^a and H=F^b. The adjunction and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] identify j_!(\bigoplus_{a+b=d}Q^a\otimes j^*F^b) with \bigoplus_{a+b=d}j_!(Q^a\otimes j^*F^b). Taking the sum of the \psi_{Q^a,F^b} defines an isomorphism in total degree d. Naturality gives \psi_{a+1,b}(j_!d_Q\otimes1)=j_!(d_Q\otimes1)\psi_{a,b} and \psi_{a,b+1}(1\otimes d_F)=j_!(1\otimes j^*d_F)\psi_{a,b}. Add the second equality with coefficient (-1)^a. The total differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] is exactly that sum, so these equalities on each coproduct insertion prove the chain equation. Replacing the differentials by chain-map components proves naturality. Each source summand has only two differential components, so this argument works for unbounded complexes.

For a flat module G, the ordinary isomorphism \psi identifies H\mapsto j_!G\otimes H with H\mapsto j_!(G\otimes j^*H). This is a composite of exact functors: j^* and j_! are exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and G\otimes- is exact by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Thus j_!G is flat by that same definition. Apply this to every Q^a. The generic ringed-slice theorem [lem-sf-ringed-open-total-tensor-kflat] says that j_! preserves K-flat complexes and K-flat resolutions, without a constant-ring or boundedness hypothesis. Apply it to O and Q\to K. It follows that j_!Q is flat-term K-flat and represents j_!K. In particular none of these claims requires completeness or a quasi-compact open.

source.place: Tag 0E8I; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YN (definition-K-flat), acyclic tensor test

proof.text: Take F=B_{n,X} in degree zero in step 3, for every n at once. This gives r_{Q,n}: (j_!Q)\otimes B_{n,X}\to j_!(Q\otimes B_{n,U}), a B_{n,X}-linear chain isomorphism: multiplying the outer coefficient a by b gives [x\otimes (ab)|_U] on both sides. Write q_{m,n}:B_{m,X}\to B_{n,X}. The two composites in the quotient-transition square send [x]\otimes a, respectively, to [x\otimes q_{m,n}(a)|_U] and [x\otimes q_{m,n}(a|_U)]; these coincide since q restricts to the quotient map on U. For a chain map v:Q\to Q', both naturality composites send [x]\otimes a to [v(x)\otimes a|_U]. For the augmentations both composites send [x] to [x\otimes1], because restriction preserves 1. Additivity, tensor balancing and uniqueness of bilinear sheafification extension [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension-uniqueness], as in steps 1-2, extend these equalities from the displayed generators to sheaves. In the strict semilinear category of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], this is exactly the condition for the component maps to form a map of complexes of systems. Their inverses commute with transitions by multiplying each commuting square by the component inverses. Hence r_Q is an isomorphism in that category, before forgetting scalar actions.

source.place: Tag 0E8I, coefficient naturality of the generator formula; explicit quotient and augmentation squares

proof.text: Localize r_Q as a system map. By [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], \mathcal R_UK is computed by (Q\otimes B_{n,U})_n; by step 4 the corresponding model for \mathcal R_X(j_!K) is ((j_!Q)\otimes B_{n,X})_n. Exact termwise J_j from [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] computes the other side, J_j\mathcal R_UK. The equivalence W^{-1}\mathcal P_O\simeq D(O) in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] applies to flat-term K-flat representatives. The chain naturality in step 5 descends along this equivalence by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]: the two model functors invert quasi-isomorphisms because their localized values compute the two displayed derived functors. Conjugating the localization of r_Q by their canonical computation comparisons gives r_K. Uniqueness in that localization property proves naturality for all derived morphisms and independence under every change of representative. Since r_Q is already an isomorphism, so is r_K; there is no selection of lifts from a family of evaluated arrows.

Evaluate at n. Its inverse is the localization of \kappa in step 2, hence the open-adjunction transpose of the unit tensored with 1. This is precisely the characterization of the inverse canonical derived open tensor map in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Both the evaluation and the original reduction model use the same Q and j_!Q, so the equality holds under the canonical computation comparisons, not merely up to an unspecified isomorphism. The constructions of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] use the ordinary strict module-system category, exact termwise open extension and restriction, and simultaneous K-flat tensor models. Our map was constructed in that category using those functors and actual coefficient tensors, with their sheafification generators and localization comparisons. Thus its representative square is the square defining this specified comparison for the simultaneous construction itself. The quotient and scalar-insertion identities are already equalities of those strict complexes in step 5 and remain so on localization. Evaluation is used here to identify the already constructed map, never to infer equality of arbitrary system arrows. No proof step used completeness or quasi-compactness.
